title: India’s Southern Kerala State Imposes ‘Fat Tax’ on Fast Food

image.attribution: Bryan Allison from Las Vegas, NV / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-2.0

main_content:
Customers in India’s southern state of Kerala will have to dig deeper into their pockets each time they want to order a juicy burger, a cheese-laced pizza, or other fast food such as doughnuts and tacos.

Vowing to combat rising levels of obesity—Kerala has the second highest levels of obesity in the country—the state government is imposing a 14.5 percent “fat tax” on fast foods sold by branded restaurants such as McDonalds and Pizza Hut.

questions.question: Why is Kerala imposing the "fat tax"?
options: To increase revenue for local businesses.
To promote healthier eating habits among the population.
To discourage the consumption of unhealthy fast foods.
To reduce the prices of traditional foods.
questions.answer: To discourage the consumption of unhealthy fast foods.

questions.question: Does Kerala have the highest levels of obesity in India?
options: Yes, it has the highest levels of obesity in the country.
No, it has the second highest levels of obesity.
Yes, it is the only state with obesity issues.
No, it has the lowest levels of obesity.
questions.answer: No, it has the second highest levels of obesity.

questions.question: What will be taxed under Kerala's "fat tax"?
options: Fresh fruits and vegetables sold in local markets.
Fast foods sold by branded restaurants such as McDonald's and Pizza Hut.
All food sold in every restaurant across Kerala.
questions.answer: Fast foods sold by branded restaurants such as McDonald's and Pizza Hut.
